Compute the aggregate loss distribution

Source: R/aggregate-distribution.R
aggregate_distribution.Rd

Evaluates the distribution of the collective aggregate loss

$$S = \sum_{i=1}^{N} X_i$$

from a tidyact_collective_risk_spec object.

The function separates the actuarial model from the computational algorithm. It never fits a distribution, never simulates the aggregate loss, and never discretizes a continuous severity implicitly.

Usage

aggregate_distribution(
  x,
  method = c("auto", "analytic", "convolution", "panjer", "fft"),
  tol = 1e-08,
  max_loss = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A tidyact_collective_risk_spec object.

method

Computational method. One of "auto", "analytic", "convolution", "panjer", or "fft".

tol

Positive finite probability tolerance smaller than one. It is used when an infinite claim-count distribution must be truncated numerically or when Panjer recursion is allowed to stop after capturing at least 1 - tol of the aggregate probability.

max_loss

Optional nonnegative finite numeric scalar giving the largest aggregate-loss value to retain in the returned grid. Probability above the retained grid is not renormalized; it is reported separately as tail_probability, together with any omitted claim-count probability.

...

Reserved for future computational controls. Additional arguments are currently rejected.

Value

An object with classes "tidyact_aggregate_distribution" and "tidyact_risk_distribution". It contains:

schema_version

Internal schema version.

method

The computational method actually used.

grid

A tibble with loss, probability, and cdf.

support

Support information for the retained grid.

tail_probability

Probability not represented on the retained grid.

model

The source collective risk specification.

label

The model label, if any.

metadata

Audit information about method selection, truncation, exactness, and numerical controls.

Details

aggregate_distribution() operates only on an already specified collective model. The probabilistic model is never changed in order to make an algorithm applicable.

In particular, if the severity distribution is continuous and no supported analytic form is available, the function stops and asks the user to apply discretize_severity() explicitly before using Panjer recursion or FFT.

Automatic method selection

With method = "auto", the function uses the following hierarchy:

  1. an implemented analytic representation for deterministic aggregate structures;

  2. Panjer recursion when the severity is on a lattice and the frequency distribution supplies valid Panjer parameters;

  3. exact finite convolution when both frequency and severity have finite discrete support;

  4. FFT when the severity is on a lattice and the frequency distribution supplies the probability operations required to truncate its count support.

If none of these conditions is satisfied, an informative error is returned.

Analytic method

The initial analytic engine handles aggregate losses that are degenerate at zero and deterministic severities. If \(X = c\) almost surely, then

$$S = cN$$

and the aggregate probabilities are obtained directly from the count distribution. Infinite count support is truncated according to tol unless max_loss supplies a tighter explicit cutoff.

Additional analytic compound families may be added later without changing the public interface.

Convolution method

The convolution engine is exact for finite claim-count support and finite discrete severity support. It evaluates

$$ P(S \in A) = \sum_n P(N=n) P(X_1+\cdots+X_n \in A) $$

by repeated finite convolution. If max_loss is supplied, the full finite distribution is evaluated first and probability above the requested cutoff is reported as tail probability.

Panjer method

For a frequency distribution in the \((a,b,0)\) class,

$$ p_n = \left(a + \frac{b}{n}\right)p_{n-1}, $$

and a lattice severity with probabilities \(f_j\), the aggregate probabilities satisfy

$$ g_0 = G_N(f_0) $$

and, for \(k \ge 1\),

$$ g_k = \frac{ \sum_{j=1}^{k} \left(a + \frac{bj}{k}\right) f_j g_{k-j} }{ 1-a f_0 }. $$

Only severity probabilities available on the lattice are used. No discretization is performed by this engine.

FFT method

FFT evaluates a finite polynomial approximation to the compound distribution. For an infinite claim-count distribution, the count support is first truncated at a quantile whose omitted probability is no greater than tol. This omitted count probability is carried explicitly into tail_probability; it is not wrapped into the retained FFT grid.

The FFT engine therefore uses the truncated count polynomial

$$ \sum_{n=0}^{n_{\max}} p_n z^n $$

rather than the full PGF. This avoids silently treating circular aliasing as aggregate probability.

Returned probabilities

The returned grid contains:

  • loss: aggregate loss amount;

  • probability: probability mass assigned to that amount;

  • cdf: cumulative probability captured on the retained grid.

The grid is intentionally not renormalized when a positive tail remains. Consequently,

$$ \sum p_s + p_{\mathrm{omitted}} = 1 $$

up to numerical tolerance. With loss-grid truncation alone, omitted mass is above the grid. FFT count truncation also omits events with large claim counts but potentially small aggregate losses (especially when zero severities are possible). Thus tail_probability is total unrepresented mass, not necessarily P(S > max(grid$loss)). VaR checks whether omitted count mass could change its selected quantile; TVaR and stop-loss reject unresolved mass.

References

Bowers, N. L., Gerber, H. U., Hickman, J. C., Jones, D. A., and Nesbitt, C. J. (1997). Actuarial Mathematics, 2nd ed. Society of Actuaries.

Klugman, S. A., Panjer, H. H., and Willmot, G. E. (2019). Loss Models: From Data to Decisions, 5th ed. Wiley.

See also

collective_risk_spec(), discretize_severity(), aggregate_moments()

Examples

frequency <- frequency_spec(
  "poisson",
  lambda = 4
)

severity <- severity_spec(
  "gamma",
  shape = 2,
  rate = 0.001
)

model <- collective_risk_spec(
  frequency,
  severity
)

# Continuous severities are never discretized implicitly.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aggregate_distribution(model)
} # }

lattice_severity <- discretize_severity(
  severity,
  step = 100
)

lattice_model <- collective_risk_spec(
  frequency,
  lattice_severity
)

aggregate_distribution(
  lattice_model,
  method = "panjer",
  tol = 1e-8
)
#> <tidyact_aggregate_distribution>
#> Method: panjer
#> Grid points: 545
#> Retained loss range: [0, 54400]
#> Captured probability: 0.9999999901
#> Tail probability: 9.871212736e-09

aggregate_distribution(
  lattice_model,
  method = "fft",
  tol = 1e-8
)
#> <tidyact_aggregate_distribution>
#> Method: fft
#> Grid points: 3142
#> Retained loss range: [0, 432000]
#> Captured probability: 0.9999999981
#> Tail probability: 1.923058379e-09
